title: The door that forgot its reader
hook: Ise found a child's brass library key in the returns. It opens the little lamp beside the door. The child remembers a voice in the lamplight. Tonight you can bring a voice back to her.

uses.action: Turn the shade towards the waiting bench
uses.reply: The child holds a place for her grandfather. Together they can examine the mark you left. The desk clerk has to bring his chair round.

uses.action: Turn the shade towards the keyhole
uses.reply: A reader outside catches the pattern through the door. The child runs out to hear what the stranger thought it meant.

question: Who could see your work from the other side of the door?

pair.title: The child with two keys
sights: A rule on the library door says every child may come in. The smallest child cannot reach the handle.
Through the middle slit a school notebook fits under the handle like a step. Someone has written Tuesday on its spine.
A page from a child's Tuesday describes a day the annual speech never mentions.

choices.action: Lower the handle and leave the notebook to its owner
choices.reply: The youngest reader comes back alone. The clerk has to ask her which account of Tuesday ought to sit on the shelf.

choices.action: Display Tuesday next to the rule
choices.reply: The clerk sees who was missing from the ceremony. The child still has to knock, and this time the clerk hears her.

pair.question: Who was missing from a promise addressed to everybody?

arrival: The girl has brought a footstool. She sets it under the lamp herself. “Can I be the one who looks first?”

title: The slip that came home wet
hook: Imani's runner found a slip plastered to a ferry rope. Somebody had drawn a little roof over the ink to keep the name dry. The boat leaves again at dusk.

uses.action: Slip the tracing under the ferry glass
uses.reply: Passengers can follow the mark while they wait. The boat takes the only lit copy away with it.

uses.action: Hang the tracing where the runner turns back
uses.reply: The runner finds the family who left the slip. The next boat leaves before they finish talking.

question: What part of a record needs to travel with its reader?

pair.title: The procession in the wrong column
sights: A carrier's name occurs in both copies of a message. Two seals mask a common route.
At the join both accounts pass the same corner. The verbs change precisely where the district clerk starts writing.
A neighbourhood drum calls people together. In the clerk's column the same people merely appear.

choices.action: Trace both accounts to the carrier
choices.reply: The runner carries one parcel back. The family can question the witness both copies depended on.

choices.action: Pin the crowd's verb beside the clerk's
choices.reply: The little roof keeps both verbs dry. The runner asks the neighbours which one belongs on tomorrow's notice.

pair.question: Whose action disappears when two sources inherit the same description?

arrival: Imani’s runner has tucked a second slip into a dry shoe. “If this one gets wet, I walk home barefoot.” She holds the lantern steady with her elbow.

title: A breath on the glass
hook: Aster promised two sisters that their father's mark would still be here by morning. One sister sees it only when the glass fogs. The other brought a cloth.

uses.action: Clear one narrow window for a close look
uses.reply: One sister finds a detail with her fingertip against the glass. Her breath hides it from the queue behind her.

uses.action: Catch the whole outline on the cold sheet
uses.reply: Both sisters stand back and see the outline. They have to lean in again to settle the smallest mark.

question: Who could check the detail after the frost returned?

pair.title: The space for a saucer
sights: A ledger records how many people ate here. No line says whose hands set the table.
A chipped rim fills a gap exactly the size of a saucer. Its fit cannot give its owner a name.
A plan of the kitchen marks where small pieces of a saucer lay by the step.

choices.action: Show the rim beside the empty name space
choices.reply: A visitor sees the work omitted by the ledger and leaves the name open.

choices.action: Follow the fragments back to the kitchen step
choices.reply: The sisters trace a lived space. They leave the list in the cold store for a second visit.

pair.question: What can an object restore to an account that it cannot name?

arrival: One sister has polished a circle in the frost. The other has saved a patch the size of her thumb. There is room for your light at the edge of both.

title: An answer after the foghorn
hook: Ruan's daughter lowered her own signal lamp into the mist. Something flashed back from a jetty the charts call empty. Her father quietly lit a second wick.

uses.action: Aim the shutter at the jetty
uses.reply: A hand flashes an answer through the mist. The next watch finds the jetty, but the channel stays dark.

uses.action: Turn the glass towards the incoming boat
uses.reply: The crew slows in time to see the mark. The distant keeper leaves a light burning for your return.

question: Whose reply could the crew see from the water?

pair.title: A light outside the ring
sights: The measured lights at the edge keep pace where the chart predicts a fall.
The same edge fits two chalk curves. The lines separate on the second wheel, which has yet to be observed.
Another rule changes how the pull is calculated in a weak field.

choices.action: Mark the second wheel before it turns
choices.reply: Ruan's daughter seals a prediction in the spare lamp. The next watch can open it against a fresh sighting.

choices.action: Hang both curves behind the observed lights
choices.reply: The boat crew can see what the two accounts share. No one can identify the cause by that fit alone.

pair.question: Where would the next observation tell the two accounts apart?

arrival: Ruan’s daughter counts to four in the dark. A pale square opens offshore on five. “Dad always stops counting on four.” She offers you the place she stood.

title: Tracks around an empty nest
hook: Elian found his chalk line trodden flat. His assistant blames the visitors. A small set of prints comes from inside the rope. They kneel at different ends of the same trail.

uses.action: Set a near window beside the small tracks
uses.reply: A watcher sees the direction of the toes. Anyone leaning in loses sight of the outer trail.

uses.action: Raise a viewing strip above the rope
uses.reply: Walkers trace both paths from a distance. The smallest impression stays in shadow.

question: Which detail would let someone question your first account of the trail?

pair.title: The gap between the tracks
sights: A series of small soft-edged pits crosses layer after layer on the tracing.
One band has no prints at all. Both sheets fit the silence, for different reasons.
An animal appears below the band and leaves no trace in the layer above.

choices.action: Walk the band to look for its edges
choices.reply: The assistant finds the layer thinning at the stream. A gap in this patch may not extend to the whole forest.

choices.action: Keep the two histories in the blind
choices.reply: A visitor can trace gradual change and a sudden disappearance without settling which made this gap.

pair.question: When could local absence support a claim far beyond the trail?

arrival: Elian’s assistant lets a beetle climb off the chalk. “He’s crossed our rope six times today. Nobody’s asked for his permit.” Something larger rustles under the blind.

title: A stamp for the night shift
hook: Corra keeps the mark from her first inspection in her pocket. The night crew has found a mark that looks exactly like it on a piece she never saw.

uses.action: Keep the comparison on the inspector's bench
uses.reply: The two marks lie side by side under a steady light. A worker finishing late waits for Corra's key.

uses.action: Put the comparison on the night cart
uses.reply: The crew takes it to the piece in question. The cart shakes, and the finest line needs a second look tomorrow.

question: What could the night crew establish that a clerk at the bench could not?

pair.title: The rack that lost a mark
sights: The loading instructions change row into a numbered slot. The ink numeral is clear.
Both sheets move the same object one place sideways. One shift happened in the instructions and the other when the clerk aligned two sets of coordinates.
Two charts put a single reference point on different grids.

choices.action: Keep the instruction with its translation
choices.reply: The night worker catches the slot change. The grid still needs its own reference mark.

choices.action: Pin the two grids to one identifiable point
choices.reply: The second crew aligns the charts. Corra asks the clerk to trace the instruction before loading again.

pair.question: Which part of a chain did the final misplaced mark fail to identify?

arrival: Corra takes the stamp out of her pocket and sets it face down. The night worker lays a bare hand beside it. Their thumbs have worn the same hollow.

title: The print that let go
hook: Lark's apprentice lifts a clean sheet. A line of tiny letters has stuck to the roller. The apprentice turns it by hand. Her missing line appears backwards in the light.

uses.action: Turn the proof to face the press crew
uses.reply: The person who set the type catches a shift in the spacing. The queue sees the page only after the doors open.

uses.action: Swing the proof out to the street
uses.reply: A street reader recognises what the crew missed. Rain freckles one edge before they draw it back inside.

question: Who could detect a change once the page moved?

pair.title: The guest in the margin
sights: A figure at the edge of a drawing points back at the officials in the centre.
The two frames share a doorway. The visitor who gets to describe it changes when the frames exchange places.
A caption presents the traveller's description as if the people being described had supplied it themselves.

choices.action: Turn the caption so the drawn figure faces its author
choices.reply: The apprentice sees who is looking back. A reader asks whose description the street still lacks.

choices.action: Leave room for a second account at the margin
choices.reply: One reader adds a location the visitor missed. The original drawing keeps its separate authorship.

pair.question: Who appears as a knower when the frame changes hands?

arrival: Lark holds a mirror to the roller. The apprentice reads her own little line backwards and laughs. “I can do that quicker than he can read it the right way.”

title: A light for the returning boat
hook: Renna's brother has sent two bearings and no signature. Last time she joined the marks without asking where he stood. Tonight a lamp burns at each end of the chart table.

uses.action: Pin the tracing to the chart table
uses.reply: A second pilot can retrace the line. The brother has to remember it once he leaves the room.

uses.action: Fit the tracing to the handboard
uses.reply: The boat crew carries it to the waterline. Its edge leaves out the most distant landmark.

question: Which change of viewpoint could shift the reading?

pair.title: Two ways to reach a neighbour
sights: A short ruler follows three inlets that the long stride jumps.
The nearest house by coastline and the nearest household by obligations are on different sides of the inlet.
A thread from one household crosses the water twice to reach the person who brings its shopping.

choices.action: Give the pilot both scales at the landing
choices.reply: The pilot can estimate the journey. The household has to say which visit is urgent.

choices.action: Begin with the household that needs the crossing
choices.reply: The boat serves the neighbour first. The pilot marks the extra distance against the tide.

pair.question: What does near measure when the route is also a relationship?

arrival: Renna has set her brother’s tea beside the chart. A drop runs down the paper and joins two islands. She moves the cup. “There. I nearly made another shortcut.”

title: The cue that nobody called
hook: Edda heard a cue after everybody had left the stage. A dresser behind the curtain says she gave it with her sleeve. The actor in the front row swears he heard a voice.

uses.action: Give the cue strip to the dresser
uses.reply: The next actor enters on the sleeve. The audience misses the gesture that made the entrance possible.

uses.action: Open the shutter towards the front row
uses.reply: The first row knows when to answer. A performer in the wings must follow their faces.

question: Who made the cue work without being seen?

pair.title: One audience with two backs
sights: A gesture in the edge of a shot changes how the spoken line lands.
At the centre, both images move at once. A single spectator must choose which face to miss.
Two screens face one another across the room. A witness facing one has their back to the other.

choices.action: Let two audience members trade accounts
choices.reply: A second telling restores the unseen gesture. The witnesses disagree about its timing.

choices.action: Run the cue again from the opposite seat
choices.reply: One spectator sees both moments in succession. The others cannot have their first surprise back.

pair.question: What did another witness make possible that a replay could not?

arrival: Edda bows to an empty seat. The dresser slips her cuff over a nail. From the back row it sounds exactly like one person trying to clap quietly.

title: A promise at closing time
hook: Tellen once chased a customer to return a coin. Tonight the same customer has brought back his old scale weight. One edge is smooth from being lent round the market.

uses.action: Keep the example at the common scale
uses.reply: Several stallholders can compare their measures. The customer must carry her basket back across the square.

uses.action: Send it along the row of stalls
uses.reply: Each seller gets a turn. The last one asks who checked it after it left Tellen's hand.

question: How could two people compare results after the measure moved?

pair.title: Oil for the last crossing
sights: The price board shows exactly when the innkeeper stopped buying oil.
The last token is in the hand of the traveller waiting for a neighbour. The board has no column for that relationship.
The midwife's need stays the same as the price rises. Two families are counting on her journey.

choices.action: Let the midwife reserve a measure
choices.reply: The next birth has light. Tellen has to explain to a stranger who can make a similar claim.

choices.action: Post the remaining supply and invite neighbours to pool tokens
choices.reply: The street can act on the shortage. A traveller who knows nobody still needs somebody to notice her.

pair.question: Which need became visible only after somebody could answer back?

arrival: The old customer rests the weight on Tellen’s open palm. “Close your fingers. Now it feels like mine.” A thin bright crescent shows between them.

title: A ribbon caught below the weir
hook: Omi finds the children's waterline ribbon on the wrong side of the gate. Her ledger says the bank stayed dry. The children know exactly which shoes got wet.

uses.action: Hang the strip at the keeper's gauge
uses.reply: The next shift can compare levels at one fixed point. The children have to bring their story uphill.

uses.action: Fasten it to the lower footbridge
uses.reply: A family sees the mark on the way home. Omi needs a second mark to relate it to the gauge.

question: What did the position of the mark let somebody claim?

pair.title: What rang before the flood
sights: A bell and a bank of open umbrellas precede each wet afternoon on the slate.
Moving the bell on the model makes one story fall apart. The dramatic sketch of the last flood still sticks in the keeper's mind.
The last crossing is painted in bright ink. Its ordinary dry neighbours barely show.

choices.action: Try the bell on a model dry day
choices.reply: The children watch the umbrellas turn without the level rising. The keeper redraws one arrow.

choices.action: Restore the dry crossings to the record
choices.reply: A strong memory now has neighbours. The cause of the flood still needs a separate test.

pair.question: Which move checks the cause and which checks what we remembered to count?

arrival: Omi is wringing out one small sock over her ledger. The figure for the dry bank has begun to run. “Let it,” says the child who wore it.

title: The second bell rope
hook: Ade's dispatch bell rang while both his hands were full. A courier shows you a second cord running into the reading room. She wants it left where readers can reach it.

uses.action: Leave the finding at the operator's dial
uses.reply: Ade can send the same mark twice. The person in the reading room has to ask him for a turn.

uses.action: Route the finding down the second cord
uses.reply: The reading room answers in its own time. Ade cannot see who pulled the cord from here.

question: When did giving someone a reply change the meaning of the message?

pair.title: The signal that costs a crossing
sights: The detailed dial tells the courier which of three roads has closed. The little dial only tells her to wait.
The two readings lead to the same choice while only one ferry is running. They diverge as soon as another road opens.
A simple cue serves a familiar route. Its success depends on which routes are available.

choices.action: Leave the simple signal at the ferry rope
choices.reply: The courier acts quickly tonight. Ade adds a hook for the day a second crossing opens.

choices.action: Carry the detailed dial to the junction
choices.reply: The next courier sees more routes. Someone must stand there long enough to read it.

pair.question: When does extra information change a decision someone can really make?

arrival: Ade holds a cup in either hand. From behind the shelves the bell rings once. The courier grins. “Go on. Put both cups down and tell me it was you.”

title: A chair behind the horn
hook: Wren set a chair behind the listening horn for a guest who hates crowds. It is empty when the song starts, but somebody has left a handkerchief over the loudest opening.

uses.action: Turn the hood towards one quiet chair
uses.reply: A visitor listens to the whole passage and chooses when to stand. A companion waits beyond the hood.

uses.action: Lift the hood for a shared listening
uses.reply: Two visitors catch different details and can compare them. The guest at the back stays near the door.

question: When did an extra listener change what could be heard?

pair.title: An answer you can hold
sights: The teller pauses just before a reply. The passage changes if the listener mistakes the pause for an ending.
The curve of a pot holds the same length of pause as the turn in a telling. The resemblance lets two people begin talking, though neither teaches the other's skill.
A hand slows at the shoulder of the vessel. A drawing preserves its outline and misses the pressure of the turn.

choices.action: Let a teller and a maker take turns
choices.reply: A listener hears the reply while watching the turn. Neither practice has to stand in for the other.

choices.action: Give each guest a separate quiet hearing
choices.reply: Each can control the pace. Wren leaves the chairs close enough for a later conversation.

pair.question: Where did a comparison open a door, and where would it erase a difference?

arrival: Wren slips the handkerchief away from the horn. A visitor in the last chair lifts one finger. Wren puts it back until the visitor is ready.

title: The model missing one roof
hook: Ivo built his sister's roof into the hillside model. She has lifted it off and left a note underneath. The path home disappears whenever the model is viewed from the door.

uses.action: Turn the model towards the doorway
uses.reply: Visitors find the roof immediately. The sister has to point out the hidden path by hand.

uses.action: Let the first visitor turn the plinth
uses.reply: The path comes into view as the model turns. Two visitors disagree about where it started.

question: What would you try from the other side of the model?

pair.title: The kitchen under the road
sights: From above, the new road is the shortest way across the island.
The plan's clean line meets a kitchen door just as someone opens it to bring a chair onto the pavement.
At dusk the people around that chair do work that no traffic map records.

choices.action: Put the chair on the plan at full scale
choices.reply: Visitors can move the road and see the detour. A driver brings her own account of the longer trip.

choices.action: Walk the proposed route before moving the line
choices.reply: Two households show the planners what the road would sever. Tomorrow's travellers still need a crossing.

pair.question: Whose loss shrinks when a planner changes scale?

arrival: Ivo’s sister pockets her little wooden roof. “You can have it back when you can get me home.” She leaves one finger on the slope to mark where she is.

title: The empty chair at the hearing
hook: Hale saved one council chair for the person described in a report. The author turned up early and sat in it. Now both of them are at the door with a claim to the light.

uses.action: Leave the lamp between the two chairs
uses.reply: Both speakers can reach the finding. Each must wait while the other turns it over.

uses.action: Face the lamp towards the public rail
uses.reply: The people affected can point to the finding themselves. The speakers have to leave their places to see their hands.

question: Who gained the power to challenge a claim when you moved the lamp?

pair.title: The minute headed Everyone
sights: The minute names the whole town as the author of a single opinion. Two people at the hearing have signed different objections.
The overlap reveals a blank for the respondent's name. An exchange can belong to a tradition while its speakers disagree.
A reply gains its force from what another person has just said. The minutes omit the first voice.

choices.action: Seat both objectors by their own accounts
choices.reply: Visitors can hear disagreement inside a shared tradition. A later speaker can add another seat.

choices.action: Give the reply its missing opening
choices.reply: The exchange becomes intelligible. Hale leaves a place to ask who had a chance to speak at all.

pair.question: When did the record allow a shared tradition to contain an argument?

arrival: Hale sits on the step to make room. From down here he can see the notes people have tucked under the rail, each folded small enough to pass through a fist.
